extracted.intended_audience: patent attorneys/practitioners before the USPTO; OED staff; Administrative Law Judges; parties to USPTO disciplinary proceedings
extracted.subtask_description: Standards, regulatory requirements, burden of proof, and sanctioning factors applied in USPTO disciplinary proceedings against registered patent practitioners. The document explains applicable Disciplinary Rules (37 C.F.R. part 10), evidentiary standards, and factors the tribunal must consider when imposing sanctions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Authority to suspend or exclude (37 C.F.R. § 10.130(a))
rubrics_metrics.description: "[T]he Commissioner may, after notice and opportunity for a hearing, suspend or exclude . . . any individual [or] attorney . . . shown to be incompetent or disreputable, who is guilty of gross misconduct, or who violates a Disciplinary Rule."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Grounds for formal discipline include incompetence, disreputability, gross misconduct, or violation of a Disciplinary Rule; disciplinary outcomes include suspension or exclusion (and other sanctions designed to protect the public interest and the integrity of the profession).

rubrics_metrics.name: Withdrawal from employment obligations (37 C.F.R. § 10.40(a))
rubrics_metrics.description: "[A] practitioner shall not withdraw from employment until the practitioner has taken reasonable steps to avoid foreseeable prejudice to the rights of the client, including giving due notice to his or her client, allowing time for employment of another practitioner, delivering to the client all papers and property to which the client is entitled, and complying with applicable laws and rules. A practitioner who withdraws from employment shall refund promptly any part of a fee paid in advance that has not been earned."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Practitioners must take concrete steps before withdrawing: notify client, allow time to retain new counsel, deliver client papers/property, comply with laws/rules, and promptly refund unearned advance fees. Failure to refund unearned fees or to take steps to avoid prejudice supports a violation finding.

rubrics_metrics.name: Failing to act competently / neglect of entrusted matters (37 C.F.R. § 10.77(c))
rubrics_metrics.description: The Disciplinary Rule provides, in pertinent part: "A practitioner shall not: (c) Neglect a legal matter entrusted to the practitioner."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Neglect includes failing to prosecute applications in a timely manner, failing to respond to client requests or communications, and other conduct evidencing lack of diligence or competence in handling client matters.

rubrics_metrics.name: Deposit of client funds in identifiable accounts (37 C.F.R. § 10.112(a)-(b))
rubrics_metrics.description: 37 C.F.R. § 10.112(a): "All funds of clients paid to a practitioner or a practitioner's firm, other than advances for costs and expenses, shall be deposited in one or more identifiable bank accounts maintained in the United States..." Section (b) describes limited exceptions and conditions for depositing practitioner funds in such accounts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Client funds (other than advances for costs/expenses) must be kept in identifiable U.S. bank accounts; practitioner's own funds should not be commingled except narrowly permitted (e.g., funds reasonably sufficient to pay bank charges or uncontested earned portions). Commingling client funds with practitioner funds is prohibited and supports disciplinary action.

rubrics_metrics.name: Maintain complete records and render accounting (37 C.F.R. § 10.112(c)(3))
rubrics_metrics.description: 37 C.F.R. § 10.112(c)(3): "Maintain complete records of all funds, securities, and other properties of a client coming into the possession of the practitioner and render appropriate accounts to the client regarding the funds, securities, or other properties."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Practitioners must keep detailed, complete records of client funds/property and provide appropriate accountings to clients; failure to maintain records or to render accounts is a specific Disciplinary Rule violation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prompt payment or delivery to client on request (37 C.F.R. § 10.112(c)(4))
rubrics_metrics.description: 37 C.F.R. § 10.112(c)(4): "Promptly pay or deliver to the client as requested by a client the funds, securities, or other properties in the possession of the practitioner which the client is entitled to receive."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Practitioners must honor client requests for return of funds/property without undue delay; refusal or delay in delivering client-entitled funds supports violation findings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mandatory character of Disciplinary Rules (37 C.F.R. § 10.20(b))
rubrics_metrics.description: The Disciplinary Rules are described as "mandatory in character and state the minimum level of conduct below which no practitioner can fall without being subject to disciplinary action."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Disciplinary Rules set mandatory baseline conduct expectations. Breach of these minimum standards can lead to disciplinary proceedings irrespective of other circumstances.

rubrics_metrics.name: Standard of proof in disciplinary proceedings (37 C.F.R. § 10.149)
rubrics_metrics.description: "In a disciplinary proceeding, the Director shall have the burden of proving his or her case by clear and convincing evidence and a respondent shall have the burden of proving any affirmative defense by clear and convincing evidence."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Director must prove allegations by the intermediate 'clear and convincing' standard (defined in the decision by citations to Addington and Cruzan). That standard requires evidence producing a firm belief or conviction in the truth of the allegations — more than preponderance but less than beyond a reasonable doubt.

rubrics_metrics.name: Factors to consider when imposing sanctions (37 C.F.R. § 10.154(b))
rubrics_metrics.description: The Regulations state that, "the following [factors] should normally be considered: (1) The public interest; (2) The seriousness of the violation of the Disciplinary Rule; (3) The deterrent effects deemed necessary; (4) The integrity of the legal profession; and (5) Any extenuating circumstances."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sanctioning is case-by-case: consider protection of public interest, gravity of the misconduct (e.g., commingling + neglect versus mere paperwork errors), need for specific and general deterrence, preservation of professional integrity, and mitigating/aggravating circumstances (motive, number of offenses, prior discipline, emotional/psychological problems, addiction, remorse, rehabilitation). Prior discipline and failure to reform weigh heavily toward harsher sanctions.

rubrics_metrics.name: ALJ procedural discretion and timing (37 C.F.R. § 10.139(c))
rubrics_metrics.description: The ALJ is authorized to set times and exercise control over the course of the proceeding; §10.139(c) expresses preference that an initial decision be issued within six months but authorizes issuance later if unusual circumstances preclude it.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The presiding ALJ may manage scheduling, prehearing motions, and briefing; significant prehearing motions or docket constraints can justify issuance of an initial decision beyond the six-month preference.

rubrics_metrics.name: Responsibilities during suspension and petition for reinstatement (37 C.F.R. §§ 10.158, 10.160) and appeal procedure (37 C.F.R. § 10.155)
rubrics_metrics.description: The decision directs attention to § 10.158 regarding responsibilities in case of suspension or exclusion, § 10.160 concerning any subsequent petition for reinstatement, and explains that appeals of an Initial Decision must be filed in duplicate with the Director within thirty (30) days and include exceptions to the ALJ's decision (§ 10.155).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Practitioners subject to suspension/exclusion must follow duties under §10.158 (e.g., representation limits, notice requirements). Petitions for reinstatement follow §10.160 procedures. Appeal of an ALJ initial decision requires filing within 30 days with required formality and exceptions; failure to appeal in accordance with §10.155 constitutes acceptance and waiver of further review.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sanctioning outcome principles (case law and equity considerations)
rubrics_metrics.description: The decision applies case law and equitable principles: disciplinary rules exist to protect the public interest and the integrity of the profession; repeated or egregious violations that reflect fundamental office-management/accounting failures (e.g., commingling + neglect) warrant exclusion and possibly permanent disbarment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When evaluating appropriate sanction, tribunals weigh prior discipline, whether prior remedial suggestions were followed, the egregiousness of misconduct (not mere paperwork), and whether lesser sanctions have failed to deter. Demonstrated lack of remediation and continued unsafe practices support exclusion rather than lesser sanctions.
